item.title: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open: Assessment of Carotid Doppler Parameters to Evaluate Volume Status: A Prospective Observational Study
item.category: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
item.description:
Objectives: Accurate assessment of volume status and fluid responsiveness is essential to guide fluid therapy, as unnecessary fluid administration may lead to fluid overload and adverse outcomes. Carotid Doppler ultrasound has emerged as a rapid, noninvasive alternative to more technically demanding echocardiographic measures. This study evaluated the utility of carotid Doppler-derived corrected flow time (FTc) and velocity-time integral (VTI), and their changes after passive leg raise (PLR), in assessing volume status and preload responsiveness.

Methods: We conducted a prospective observational study during Ramadan at a tertiary academic medical center. A total of 202 participants were enrolled, including 103 fasting individuals assessed during presumed relative dehydration and after rehydration, and 99 nonfasting hydrated controls. Carotid Doppler measurements of FTc, VTI, and Vmax were obtained before and after PLR. Diagnostic performance of percent changes in FTc (ΔFTc) and VTI (ΔVTI) was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.

Results: Participants in the fasting group underwent a mean fasting duration of 12.4 ± 1.1 hours and consumed a mean of 920 ± 352 mL of fluid after breaking the fast. PLR induced significantly greater increases in FTc and VTI during presumed relative dehydration. A ≥10% increase in VTI was observed in 57.2% of presumed relative dehydrated participants compared with 26.3% of hydrated controls and 20.4% of rehydrated participants. Similarly, a ≥5% increase in FTc was observed in 47.6%, 17.2%, and 22.3% of participants, respectively. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate discriminatory performance for presumed relative dehydration, with areas under the curve of 0.708 for ΔVTI and 0.715 for ΔFTc. Optimal cutoff values were 5.92% for ΔVTI and 5.05% for ΔFTc.

Conclusion: Carotid Doppler-derived FTc and VTI are promising noninvasive markers of volume status and preload responsiveness. ΔVTI demonstrated greater sensitivity, whereas ΔFTc provided higher specificity, supporting the potential role of carotid Doppler ultrasound as a practical bedside tool for hemodynamic assessment.

Farhat H, Abou Dagher G, Zaatari T, Makki M, Tamim H, Bou Chebl R

item.title: Crit Care Med: Association of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Radiographic Findings Identified by Machine Learning and Outcomes of Patients Receiving Invasive Mechanical Ventilation
item.description:
Objectives: To determine whether predictions from a deep learning model that identifies acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) findings on chest radiographs (CXRs) can also predict clinical outcomes beyond traditional indicators of hypoxemia and illness severity.

Design: Retrospective cohort study.

Setting: Single academic medical center.

Intervention: None.

Patients: Adult patients with CXRs performed at the time of invasive mechanical ventilation initiation.

Methods and main results: We applied a deep learning model that was previously trained to identify bilateral airspace opacities consistent with ARDS to CXRs of 6591 patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. The resulting ARDS-CXR scores were evaluated for their ability to discriminate risk of 28-day mortality and their association with 28-day mortality and time to extubation after adjusting for a patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV. The median ARDS-CXR score was -2.09, corresponding to an ARDS probability of 15%, and 1089 (17%) patients had a positive score, corresponding to an ARDS probability above 50%. Twenty-eight-day mortality was 35.1% among patients with a positive score and 13.5% among patients with a negative score. ARDS-CXR scores below the ARDS threshold also stratified risk, with mortality increasing from 12.8% at a score of -2 to 19.9% at -1 and 27.5% at 0. The ARDS-CXR score area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve was 0.68 (95% CI, 0.66-0.70) for predicting 28-day mortality, whereas the Pao2/Fio2 AUROC was 0.64 (95% CI, 0.62-0.66). After adjusting for either the patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV, a 1-point increase in the ARDS-CXR score was significantly associated with higher 28-day mortality or prolonged time to extubation.

Conclusions: A deep learning-derived ARDS-CXR score quantifying radiographic findings of ARDS independently predicted mortality and ventilator outcomes beyond hypoxemia and illness severity. Algorithmically derived markers of lung injury severity from chest imaging could be used to support clinical care decisions, predictive enrichment in research studies, or incorporated into a future ARDS definition.

Zhong Y, Nuppnau M, Farzaneh N, Ansari S, Sjoding MW
Journal Article

item.title: Crit Care Med: Brachial-to-Radial Pressure Gradient in Critically Ill Patients Treated With Vasoactive Agents: A Prospective Observational Study
item.description:
Objectives: To determine the incidence of a significant noninvasive brachial-to-radial arterial pressure gradient (NIBR-APG) and its clinical associations in critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents.

Design: Prospective, multicenter, observational study.

Setting: Thirteen ICUs in Poland.

Patients: Adult ICU patients with radial arterial catheters receiving vasoactive agents hospitalized between April 2025 and July 2025.

Interventions: None.

Measurements and main results: Invasive radial mean arterial pressure (MAP) and noninvasive brachial MAP were measured twice and averaged. A NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg was predefined as clinically significant. Baseline characteristics, hemodynamic variables, and outcomes were recorded. Among 303 patients, 49.5% were surgical admissions and 33.3% had septic shock. The median NIBR-APG was 4.5 mm Hg (interquartile range, 0.0-10.0 mm Hg). Fifty-six patients (18.4%) exhibited a NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg. Compared with patients without a significant gradient, these patients received higher norepinephrine-equivalent doses (0.23 vs. 0.10 µg/kg/min), had higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (11 vs. 10), prolonged capillary refill time (3.0 vs. 2.5 s), and higher lactate concentrations (2.7 vs. 1.3 mmol/L). In multivariable analysis, only vasoactive drug dose was independently associated with NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg (odds ratio, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.12-2.52). ICU mortality was higher in patients with significant gradients (48.0% vs. 30.1%).

Conclusions: Nearly one in five critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents demonstrated a clinically significant NIBR-APG. The presence of this gradient was independently associated with higher vasoactive drug requirements and was accompanied by greater illness severity and higher ICU mortality.

Putowski Z, Gawda R, Czarnik T, Królicki T, Trzebicka J, Zawadka M

item.title: Crit Care Med: Comparative Analysis of Tracheal Intubation-Associated Cardiac Arrest in 2015-2023: A Report From the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children Multicenter Registry
item.description:
Objectives: To determine the contemporary incidence of tracheal intubation-associated cardiac arrest (TI-CA) in critically ill children and identify potentially modifiable factors to prevent TI-CA in PICUs and pediatric cardiac ICUs (PCICUs).

Design: Retrospective cohort study.

Setting: Seventy international PICUs and PCICUs.

Patients: Critically ill children requiring tracheal intubation in PICUs and PCICUs.

Interventions: Tracheal intubation data were prospectively collected for all initial intubations in 68 PICUs and PCICUs from January 2015 to December 2023 using the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children registry.

Measurements and main results: TI-CA was defined as CA occurrence or receipt of chest compressions for at least 1 minute within 20 minutes of endotracheal tube placement. TI during ongoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation was not considered TI-CA. A total of 27,773 TIs were evaluated, with TI-CA reported in 1.2% (n = 331). Pre-TI oxygenation failure and shock were associated with higher odds of TI-CA (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.29; 95% CI, 1.81-2.89 and aOR, 4.67; 95% CI, 3.68-5.92, respectively). Each additional TI attempt required was associated with increased odds of TI-CA (aOR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.56-1.85, for each attempt). Use of ketamine (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.49-0.82), propofol (aOR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.27-0.72), neuromuscular blockade (aOR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.49-0.91), and video laryngoscopy (aOR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.6-0.97) were associated with lower odds of TI-CA. Mediation analysis indicated that 13% of video laryngoscopy's protective effect was due to a reduction in TI attempt counts. The protective effects of ketamine, propofol, and neuromuscular blockade were minimally mediated by reduced TI attempt counts (5%, 4%, and 7%).

Conclusions: TI-CA occurred in 1.2% of TIs performed in the PICUs. Odds of TI-CA increased incrementally with successive TI attempts. Video laryngoscopy was protective against TI-CA. Mediation analysis revealed that reduced TI attempts accounted for 13% of the protective benefit associated with video laryngoscopy.

Padiyath A, Padiyath F, Berg RA, Napolitano N, Nadkarni V, Shults J
Journal Article

item.title: Crit Care: Clinical prediction models in cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description:
Purpose: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) is a frequent postoperative complication associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Clinical prediction models (CPM) may identify high-risk patients enabling targeted preventive interventions and improved outcomes. The objective of the study was to identify available CPMs for the risk of developing CSA-AKI and summarize their performance.

Methods: A systematic search of studies published in Pubmed, Scopus, the Chocrane Library and Web of Science was conducted, including studies that developed or validated CPMs for CSA-AKI in adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. Data were extracted by two independent reviewers. Summary measures of diagnostic performance were calculated when feasible using random-effects models. Calibration and sensitivity analyses were also performed.

Results: The pooled incidence of CSA-AKI was 26.3% (95% CI, 26.0-26.4), whereas CSA-AKI requiring renal replacement therapy (CSA-AKI RRT) occurred in 2.2% of patients (95% CI, 2.1-2.2). Among validated CPMs, Thakar 2005 demonstrated the best predictive performance for CSA-AKI RRT: pooled AUC 0.80 (95% CI, 0.77-0.82), sensitivity of 0.87, and a specificity of 0.49 at a threshold of ≥ 3 points. Calibration analyses indicated underestimation of risk. The Mehta 2006 and Wijeysundera 2007 models also demonstrated good discrimination. Discrimination for the prediction of milder stages of CSA-AKI was poorer, but newer models such as the Demirjian 2022 model showed promising performance.

Conclusion: Accurate and well-validated CPMs can facilitate risk stratification for CSA-AKI which can influence clinical practice and research. Thakar 2005 demonstrated very good discrimination for predicting CSA-AKI RRT, whereas more validation studies for the prediction of milder stages of CSA-AKI are warranted.

Lasa-Berasain P, Torrecilla Ugarte A, Juárez-Vela R, Ibánez-Beróiz B, Ansotegui Hernández A, Sádaba R
Journal Article, Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis

item.title: Crit Care: Mucormycosis in critically ill patients: a 9-year multicenter cohort study of clinical features, management, and 90-day outcomes
item.description:
Background: Mucormycosis is a rare but life-threatening invasive fungal infection that primarily affects immunocompromised patients. Data on its presentation, management, and prognosis in the intensive care unit setting remain scarce. We aimed to evaluate 90-day mortality and to explore clinical, microbiological, therapeutic, and immunological factors associated with outcome in critically ill patients with mucormycosis.

Methods: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included patients diagnosed with mucormycosis and admitted to the ICUs of the Hospices Civils de Lyon between January 2014 and July 2023. Patients were identified through mycological records and hospital discharge codes. Univariable analysis and multivariable Cox model were performed to identify factors associated with 90-day mortality.

Results: Among 43 patients included, hematological malignancy and trauma were the most common underlying conditions (26% each), followed by solid organ transplantation (21%), and burns (16%). Cutaneous forms (49%) predominated, especially among trauma and burn patients, while pulmonary and rhinocerebral forms were mostly observed in previously immunocompromised individuals. The number of mucormycosis diagnoses increased nearly threefold over the study period, paralleling the implementation of Mucorales-specific polymerase chain reaction. Antifungal therapy was initiated in 39 patients (91%); first-line treatment was liposomal amphotericin B in 32 (74%), at a median maximum dose of 7.5 [3.5-9.4] mg/kg/day, and 12 (28%) received a combination therapy. The 90-day mortality was 47%. In the multivariable Cox model, older age, hematological malignancy, and a higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score at diagnosis were independently associated with mortality, while lower liposomal amphotericin B dosing was associated with mortality in univariable analysis. In eight patients without previous immunosuppression and uncontrolled disease, immune monitoring was performed and revealed decreased monocyte HLA-DR expression at 4556 [4194-6936] Ab/c, in favor of injury-induced immunosuppression. Among them, six patients received interferon-gamma as immunotherapy; four responded immunologically and survived.

Conclusions: Mucormycosis in critically ill patients is associated with high mortality, particularly in those with hematological malignancies. Polymerase chain reaction-based diagnostics may allow earlier detection, and immune monitoring could help identify high-risk patients, particularly in trauma and burn settings.

Bidar F, Maamcha S, Tirard-Collet P, Richard JC, Friggeri A, Fellahi JL

item.title: Chest: Adherence to Non-Invasive Ventilation in a Provincial Cohort of Children
item.description:
Background: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) adherence is critical to its effectiveness, yet no standardized pediatric definition of "optimal" adherence exists, and population-level data are scarce.

Research question: What are adherence patterns to NIV in children, and which factors are associated with adherence in a provincial longitudinal cohort?

Study design and methods: Canadian retrospective longitudinal cohort study linking records from the Ontario Ventilator Equipment Pool to health administrative databases. We identified children <18 years prescribed NIV with telemonitoring (2020 to 2022) and ≥1 month of data. The adherence definitions explored were the adult definition of ≥4 hours/day (primary) and measures of any daily use, daily NIV hours, and data missingness ("days not used" = 0 hours recorded; "days no data" = no signal). Mixed-effects regression models were used to explore adherence factors.

Results: We included 237 children (mean age 12.9 years; 61% male) with 3,685 person-months of NIV data (median 13 [IQR 8-24]). Across person-months, mean adherence by the ≥4-hours/day definition was 69.6%. Child-level monthly mean (SD) adherence was 59% (32%) by this definition, and 68% (26%) for any use. Mean (SD) daily use when used was 7.5 (3.2) hours. Monthly "days not used" and "no data" averaged 5.1 (6.4) and 4.4 (5.0) days, respectively. Greater adherence was associated with younger age (2-percentage-point decrease per year increase; 95% CI, 1-3), having ≥3 complex chronic conditions vs none (14 percentage-points higher; 95% CI, 3-26), and longer time prescribed NIV (2-percentage-point increase per year; 95% CI, 1-3).

Interpretation: NIV adherence was moderate across definitions, with higher adherence among younger children, greater medical complexity, and those using therapy longer, highlighting the need for pediatric-specific adherence targets and home NIV support strategies.

Kendzerska T, Pizzuti R, Talarico R, Gershon AS, Rose L, Amin R
Journal Article
Full text · PubMed

item.title: Resuscitation: Comparison of delivery room wrist versus earlobe pulse oximetry in newborns: A randomized controlled trial
item.description:
Objective: Rapid acquisition of reliable pulse oximetry signals in delivery room is challenging due to transitional circulation, low peripheral perfusion, motion artifact, vernix, and skin edema. This randomized controlled trial compared right earlobe and right wrist pulse oximetry to determine differences in time to reliable signal acquisition.

Methods: Pregnant women at ≥34 weeks gestation were randomized before delivery. Pulse oximetry probe was applied to either the right earlobe or right wrist immediately after birth using sensor-to-oximeter-first technique with Masimo® SET® rainbow® Radical-7® CO-Oximeter®. The primary outcome was time from completion of sensor application to reliable display of oxygen saturation and heart rate. Secondary outcomes included time from birth to start of sensor application, sensor application time, time from birth to reliable signal, perfusion index, and number of probe reapplications.

Results: Ninety-six neonates were randomized, with 48 in each group. Time from completion of sensor application to reliable signal was similar between ear and wrist groups (67.1±41.4 vs 74.5±48.2 seconds; mean difference -7.4 seconds; 95% CI -25.6 to 10.8; P=0.42). Sensor application time was shorter in ear group (mean difference -16.3 seconds; 95% CI -17.7 to -14.9; P<0.001), resulting in shorter time from birth to reliable signal (mean difference -28.8 seconds; 95% CI -53.9 to -3.7; P=0.02). Perfusion index was lower, and reapplication rates were higher in ear group.

Conclusion: Time to reliable signal acquisition after probe placement did not differ between the earlobe and wrist. Further studies using neonatal-specific ear probes are warranted.

Kumar S, Naranje K, Singh A, Verma A, Paul A, Roy A
Journal Article
Full text · PubMed

item.title: Lancet: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials
item.description:
Background: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis.

Methods: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting.

Findings: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns.

Interpretation: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

Funding: Novartis.

Wiendl H, Bermel R, Airas L, Chitnis T, Nakahara J, Williams M
Journal Article

item.title: Drug Alcohol Depend: The impact of α3β4 partial agonist AT-1001 on oxycodone withdrawal
item.description:
Purpose: Opioid withdrawal remains a major barrier to successful treatment of opioid use disorder. Non-opioid treatments such as clonidine and lofexidine reduce acute somatic symptoms but do not address affective and protracted withdrawal signs. Neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs), particularly the α3β4⁎ subtype, are a promising alternative target implicated in opioid withdrawal. Here we investigated whether AT-1001, a high-affinity α3β4⁎ partial agonist, reduces somatic and affective signs of oxycodone withdrawal in mice.

Experimental approach: Male and female C57BL/6J mice were rendered dependent on oxycodone (60mg/kg/day) or vehicle (0.9% saline) via a 7-day osmotic minipump infusion. Twenty-four hours after minipump removal, mice received an acute subcutaneous injection of vehicle, lofexidine (0.5mg/kg), or AT-1001 (0.3, 0.9, or 3mg/kg), followed by assessment of somatic withdrawal signs. In a separate cohort of oxycodone-dependent mice, animals received the highest dose of AT-1001 or lofexidine and were assessed two weeks post-minipump removal for mechanical sensitivity and anxiety-like behaviors (light/dark box assay).

Key results: Our results showed that AT-1001 dose-dependently reduced somatic withdrawal signs in oxycodone-treated mice. In contrast to lofexidine, AT-1001 attenuated mechanical hypersensitivity and anxiety-like behavior compared to the vehicle group in oxycodone-dependent mice. Furthermore, AT-1001 had no significant effect on oxycodone-induced antinociception, as evaluated in the warm-water immersion assay.

Conclusion and implications: . Our findings suggest that AT-1001 effectively reduces oxycodone withdrawal signs without altering its antinociceptive effects. This supports α3β4⁎ partial agonists as promising candidates for further development as a safer and more comprehensive opioid withdrawal treatment.

Contreras KM, Palamar A, Buzzi B, Oros A, Buttar B, Damaj M
Journal Article
Full text · PubMed

item.title: JAMA: Pregnancy Outcomes After Living Kidney Donation
item.description:
Importance: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear.

Objective: To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors.

Design, setting, and participants: This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth.

Results: The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52).

Conclusions and relevance: In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

Wang C, Naylor KL, McArthur E, King JA, Sontrop JM, Beyene J
Journal Article
Full text · PubMed

item.title: Chest: Diagnostic Contribution of Endobronchial Optical Coherence Tomography in the Multidisciplinary Diagnosis of Interstitial Lung Disease
item.description:
Background: Less-invasive, lower-risk alternatives to surgical lung biopsy (SLB) have emerged for interstitial lung disease (ILD) diagnosis, such as transbronchial lung cryobiopsy (TBLC) and Envisia Genomic Classifier (EGC), but suffer from limited sampling and simplified binomial classification, respectively. Endobronchial optical coherence tomography (EB-OCT) is a low-risk, large-volume bronchoscopic imaging modality with microscopic resolution, which accurately detects features and patterns for ILD diagnosis as previously validated against SLB.

Research question: How does EB-OCT contribute to ILD diagnosis and diagnostic confidence at multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) when paired with clinically indicated TBLC and EGC?

Study design and methods: Patients with low-confidence ILD diagnosis clinically referred for both TBLC with EGC were enrolled to undergo concurrent EB-OCT imaging. Each modality was interpreted independently by blinded pathologists. Separate MDD sessions were conducted at two independent sites, including one without prior EB-OCT experience.

Results: Fifteen patients were included (9 male; mean age: 70.6 years) with final diagnoses of UIP/IPF (n=5), secondary UIP (n=2), and various non-UIP ILDs (n=8) in agreement at both MDDs. EB-OCT provided diagnostic data that was in agreement with final MDD diagnosis for 100% of subjects (15/15), including in the 40% of subjects (6/15) where TBLC was non-diagnostic. In the subjects where TBLC yielded diagnostic data (60%, 9/15), EB-OCT diagnosis was in agreement. EB-OCT combined with TBLC/EGC increased diagnostic confidence and/or narrowed the differential diagnosis from baseline clinical/radiologic data review in all subjects, with replication across both independent MDDs.

Interpretation: In this pilot study, we demonstrate EB-OCT is a safe, large-volume imaging method that detects microscopic features and patterns for ILD diagnosis, which increases diagnostic confidence in the context of MDD and complements TBLC and EGC. Future multicenter studies are needed to further validate these findings.

Arao RK, Yamamoto S, Nandy S, Sharma A, Lee J, Berigei SR
Journal Article
Full text · PubMed

item.title: Chest: Determinants of lung cancer screening follow-up care in community care settings: A qualitative multi-case study in the ACCELL trial
item.description:
Background: Adherence to lung cancer screening (LCS) follow-up is essential to achieve mortality benefits from screening. However, population-based studies demonstrate follow-up is <50% in clinical settings. Determinants (barriers and facilitators) of LCS follow-up in community settings are under-studied.

Research question: What are determinants of LCS follow-up in community settings?

Study design and methods: This qualitative multi-case study informed a pre-post intervention trial, testing pragmatic interventions to address LCS follow-up in community settings. We conducted rapid ethnographic assessments (REA) through virtual and in person site visits of LCS delivery in three community-based healthcare systems in Washington state. Additionally at the two future intervention sites, we conducted provider and patient interviews. Interview transcripts were analyzed using Rapid Group Analysis Process. All data were triangulated according to Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research and National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities Research Framework domains.

Results: Twenty-eight organizational leaders, providers, and staff participated in REA. Thirty-one patients and 15 providers from the future intervention sites participated in interviews. Determinants of LCS follow-up in the intervention domain included role of primary care, LCS complexity and care process standardization. In the inner setting domain (organization and clinic), screening prioritization, EHR use, radiology support, and context of wellness visits affected LCS. The main theme in the outer setting domain was the influence of social determinants of health on LCS. In the individuals domain, shared beliefs in LCS and LCS education and information sharing were key. In the process implementation domain, clinical champions and use of data and metrics were crucial.

Interpretation: Integrated findings suggest determinants related to LCS complexity, care fragmentation, socioeconomic status and language, and limitations of PCPs could be overcome through more centralized approaches. However, increased use of EHR tools, increased education and standardizing LCS performance metrics may enable follow-up in decentralized settings.

Clinical trials registration: NCT06324110.

item.title: Lancet: Efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease (RISE UP): a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
item.description:
Background: Persistent haemolytic anaemia and recurrent vaso-occlusion drive complications and accelerate mortality in sickle cell disease. Mitapivat, an oral allosteric activator of pyruvate kinase, increases ATP and decreases 2,3-DPG with the potential to improve haemolytic anaemia and reduce sickling. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease.

Methods: We report results from RISE UP, a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial from 69 sites across 15 countries. Patients older than 16 years with anaemia and recurrent sickle cell pain crises were randomly assigned (2:1) to either mitapivat 100 mg or placebo twice a day using permuted-block randomisation. Primary endpoints, assessed in all randomly assigned patients, were haemoglobin response (≥1·0 g/dL increase in average haemoglobin concentration from week 24 to week 52 compared with baseline) and annualised rate of sickle cell pain crises. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05031780, and the open-label extension is ongoing.

Findings: A total of 207 patients were randomly assigned to mitapivat (138 [67%]) or placebo (69 [33%]). 56 (41%) of 138 patients in the mitapivat group had a haemoglobin response, compared with two (3%) of 69 patients on placebo (adjusted difference 38%, 95% CI 29-47; two-sided p<0·0001). The annualised rate (95% CI) of sickle cell pain crises was 2·6 (2·3-3·0) for mitapivat and 3·1 (2·6-3·6) for placebo (two-sided p=0·1213). Serious adverse events were reported in 28 (20%) patients on mitapivat and 20 (29%) patients on placebo; one (1%) patient and 0 patients, respectively, were deemed treatment related.

Interpretation: Mitapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, with a novel mechanism that ameliorates haemolytic anaemia, has the potential to be an effective and convenient disease-modifying treatment for people with sickle cell disease.

Funding: Agios Pharmaceuticals.

item.title: Drug Alcohol Depend: Safety and efficacy of psilocybin-assisted therapy for alcohol use disorder: Open-label extension of a phase II randomized controlled trial
item.description:
Background: Psilocybin-assisted therapy (PAT) has shown promise for alcohol use disorder (AUD) in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). It remains unknown, however, whether patients derive additional benefit when psilocybin is administered open-label after completion of blinded treatment. Here, we report safety and efficacy outcomes from an open-label extension of a Phase II RCT of PAT for AUD (NCT02061293).

Methods: Fifty-nine adults with AUD received a single open-label administration of psilocybin (25-40mg/70kg) accompanied by four hours of manualized therapy. During the preceding double-blind phase, 29 of these participants had received psilocybin (psilocybin-psilocybin group; PP) and 30 had received the active placebo diphenhydramine (diphenhydramine-psilocybin group; DP). Mixed-effects models for repeated measures evaluated alcohol consumption (percent heavy drinking days [PHDD], drinks per day [DpD], and percent drinking days [PDD]), alcohol craving, abstinence self-efficacy, and treatment readiness across a four-month follow-up.

Results: Psilocybin was well tolerated, and no serious adverse events occurred. Among participants with higher drinking intensity at extension entry, decreases in PHDD, DpD, and PDD were observed at Month 1 but returned to entry levels thereafter. Craving, abstinence self-efficacy, and treatment readiness improved in both PP and DP groups one week after administration, with variable trajectories thereafter.

Discussion: After completion of the double-blind trial, a single open-label psilocybin administration was associated with maintained remission among most participants who entered abstinent and with acute but largely transient reductions among those who were still drinking heavily. Whether the limited durability reflects the lower intensity of extension treatment, the relative treatment resistance of residual drinking, differences in motivation, or other design-related factors cannot be determined from these data.

Clinical trial registration: NCT02061293, A Double-Blind Trial of Psilocybin-Assisted Treatment of Alcohol Dependence, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02061293.

Pagni BA, Ross S, Mennenga S, Bhatt S, Zeifman RJ, Petridis PD

item.title: Drug Alcohol Depend: Neighborhood violence, visible drug activity, and substance use among urban youth: Mental health and community factors
item.description:
Background: Adolescent substance use and exposure to neighborhood violence frequently co-occur in U.S. urban settings, particularly among racially minoritized and low-income youth. Despite shared exposure to environmental risk, some adolescents report low to no substance use. Guided by the adverse community experiences and resilience framework, this study identified classes of neighborhood risk and substance use among urban adolescents and examined whether emotional, behavioral, community, and demographic factors differentiated profile membership.

Methods: Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 743 adolescents aged 13-21 residing in a large Northeastern U.S. city. Five dichotomous indicators (witnessed neighborhood violence, seen drugs sold in their neighborhood, and lifetime vaping, alcohol, and marijuana use) were analyzed using latent class analysis. Multinomial logistic regression examined associations between class membership and emotional, behavioral, community, and demographic factors.

Results: A three-class solution was retained: No Neighborhood Risk Exposure/Low or No Substance Use (34%), High Exposure/Low or No Use (40%), and High Exposure/Polysubstance Use (26%). Compared with the High Exposure/Low or No Use class, the No Neighborhood Risk Exposure/Low or No Use class reported higher neighborhood support and lower racial discrimination, missing school, and suicidal thoughts. The High Exposure/Polysubstance Use class differed from the High Exposure/Low or No Use class primarily by higher depressive symptoms.

Conclusions: Low substance use should not be interpreted as low need among adolescents exposed to neighborhood risk. Adolescent health and well-being efforts should assess mental health distress, suicidal ideation, racial discrimination-related experiences, and school disengagement alongside substance use.

item.title: Drug Alcohol Depend: Prejudicial essentialist bias in cognitive neuroscience studies with people who use drugs
item.description:
Objectives: Professional judgement can be biased (or prejudiced) by the incidental social characteristics of marginalised clients. Perhaps unexpectedly, psychologists have been hypothesised to express prejudicial essentialist bias in their writing; disproportionately invoking pathological constitutional deficits to explain observed differences in study participants with marginalised social characteristics.

Methods: To test whether this bias exists in cognitive neuroscience publications, 67 case-controlled studies reporting lower cognitive task performance in people who use drugs (PWUD) versus controls were collated. The percentage of explanations of PWUD's performance using essentialist terms ('deficits', 'dysfunction', 'impairments') versus neutral-agnostic terms ('difference', 'change', 'alteration' etc.) were tested for associations with PWUD's social characteristics, study effect size and publication year.

Results: Deficit descriptions were used on 64% of occasions and were significantly associated with PWUD's social characteristics including their mean age (r = 0.40), percent male (r = 0.24), primary drug (η2 = 0.24), and dependence severity indexed by their recruitment from clinical sources (η2 = 0.12) and characterisation using clinical diagnostics (η2 = 0.15); but not with the effect size of the task performance difference (r = 0.029) or publication year (r = -0.18).

Conclusions: Psychologists' unwarranted causal inference that task performance differences arise from constitutional pathogenic origins may be prejudiced by the incidental social characteristics of their PWUD sample. This bias may be explained by professional incentives, journal remit and author training influencing narrative construction. Solutions for the bias may involve meta-scientific auditing, strengthening of language guidelines, and critical reflective practice implemented through positionality statements in quantitative research.

item.title: Drug Alcohol Depend: Accuracy of self-reported e-cigarette nicotine strength in young adults (18-26) and adults (27-54) who vape and differences in their preferences for nicotine strength and flavor
item.description:
Purpose: To examine the accuracy of self-reported nicotine strength and differences in nicotine strength and flavor preferences between young adults and adults who vape. Accurate assessment of nicotine exposure is essential for understanding vaping behavior and informing public health research, yet the reliability of self-reported nicotine strength remains unclear.

Methods: We recruited 61 young adults (18-26) and 65 adults (27-54). Participants reported the nicotine strength of their vaping products (high vs. low) and provided product samples for laboratory analysis. Nicotine concentrations in the samples were measured using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Participants were asked about their preferred flavor and whether they prioritize nicotine strength or flavor when purchasing a product.

Results: The agreement between self-reported and laboratory-derived nicotine strengths (Cohen's kappa) was 0.73 for young adults and 0.71 for adults. More young adults used high-nicotine products (≥24mg/mL) than adults (50.8% vs. 30.8%; p = 0.022). Most participants in both age groups used fruit/sweet products more than non-sweet (tobacco/menthol). However, nicotine strength was more frequently identified as the primary factor influencing product choice than flavor.

Conclusion: Among young adults who vaped regularly in this sample, self-reported nicotine strength showed substantial agreement with laboratory-derived low/high nicotine-strength categories, supporting its use for broad classification in research settings. Nicotine strength appeared to be more important for young adults than flavor. This study provides novel evidence that nicotine concentration plays a central role in vaping behavior and highlights the importance of regulating nicotine strength alongside flavors to reduce vaping rates among young people.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Rapid bolus versus 3-h continuous infusion of 3% hypertonic saline for acute symptomatic hyponatremia
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Background and objectives: Hyponatremia is a common electrolyte disorder in emergency care that requires careful clinical management. Sodium correction, safety, 30-day hyponatremia-related hospital readmission, and mortality were compared between a 20-min rapid intermittent bolus (RIB) and a 3-h slow continuous infusion (SCI) of 3% hypertonic saline in adults with acute symptomatic hyponatremia.

Methods: This prospective cohort study included 58 adults presenting to the emergency department with acute symptomatic hyponatremia patients were assigned to RIB (20 min; n = 29) or SCI (3 h; n = 29) using a study-specific allocation list. Sodium kinetics through 24 h, safety, and 30-day outcomes were assessed using ANCOVA, repeated-measures ANOVA, multivariable regression, and ROC analysis.

Results: Twenty-four-hour sodium correction was comparable between groups. One overcorrection occurred with SCI; no osmotic demyelination syndrome occurred. Thirty-day hyponatremia-related hospital readmission was 13.8% with RIB and 41.4% with SCI (p = 0.019); In an exploratory adjusted analysis, SCI was associated with higher adjusted odds (aOR) of readmission (aOR:7.04; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.56-31.80; p = 0.011). Higher baseline Glasgow Coma Scale score was associated with lower 30-day-all-cause mortality (aOR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.17-0.88; p = 0.025). A baseline sodium cutoff of ≤115.5 mmol/L showed exploratory discrimination for second dose requirement with an area under the curve of 0.754.

Conclusion: Both RIB and SCI protocols demonstrated similar short-term sodium correction, with few observed adverse events. The difference in 30-day hyponatremia-related hospital readmission and exploratory associations involving baseline neurological status and serum sodium require confirmation in larger studies.

item.title: N Engl J Med: Ravulizumab in IgA Nephropathy - Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial
item.category: The New England journal of medicine
item.description:
Background: In patients with IgA nephropathy, complement activation drives glomerular inflammation, which leads to hematuria, proteinuria, and nephron loss. Ravulizumab is a terminal complement inhibitor that prevents formation of C5a and C5b-9.

Methods: In this phase 3 trial, we enrolled adults with IgA nephropathy who had an estimated glomerular filtration rate of at least 30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and proteinuria (24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio [with protein and creatinine both measured in grams] of ≥0.75 or total urinary protein excretion of ≥1.0 g per day), despite standard therapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of either ravulizumab or placebo every 8 weeks. In the prespecified interim analysis, the primary efficacy end point was the change from baseline in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 34. Safety was also assessed.

Results: In all, 485 patients underwent randomization, with 240 patients assigned to the ravulizumab group and 245 to the placebo group; 352 patients (176 in each group) were included in the interim analysis. In the ravulizumab group, the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at baseline and at week 34 was 1.56 and 0.83, respectively; in the placebo group, it was 1.60 and 1.48, respectively. At week 34, a significant reduction in the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio was observed with ravulizumab (-46.6%) as compared with the reduction observed with placebo (-5.6%), corresponding to an adjusted geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio that was 43.4% (99% confidence interval, 30.1 to 54.2) lower with ravulizumab than with placebo (P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 69.5% of the patients receiving ravulizumab and in 75.8% of those receiving placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 4.6% and 9.0%, respectively. No meningococcal infections or deaths occurred.

Conclusions: In adults with IgA nephropathy, ravulizumab resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo at week 34. (Funded by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease Unit; I CAN ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06291376; EU Clinical Trials number, 2023-507851-31-00.).

item.title: N Engl J Med: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy
item.category: The New England journal of medicine
item.description:
Background: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL.

Methods: In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria.

Results: A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups.

Conclusions: Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Clinical Walking Speed, Free-Living Walking Cadence, and All-Cause Mortality
item.description:
Importance: Walking speed has been shown to be associated with mortality and is conventionally obtained from short walking tests in clinical settings. Free-living walking parameters such as walking cadence can be derived from accelerometers.

Objective: To examine whether walking parameters measured in clinical and free-living settings are associated with comparable discriminative ability for all-cause mortality risk.

Design, setting, and participants: This population-based cohort study, the Whitehall II accelerometer substudy in the UK, included a baseline from January 2012 to December 2013 and follow-up through August 19, 2024. The study included participants with valid accelerometer data, clinical walking speed, covariates, and electronic health records information. Analyses were performed between September 2025 and February 2026.

Exposures: Clinical walking speed in meters per second was obtained from a 2.44-m walking test, and 2 free-living metrics of walking cadence in steps per minute (the median walking cadence and the 95th percentile walking cadence) were derived from 9 days of wrist-worn accelerometer data.

Main outcomes and measures: All-cause mortality was ascertained from a British national mortality register. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for all-cause mortality. Discriminative ability was assessed using the Harrel concordance index (C index).

Results: A total of 4067 participants (mean [SD] age, 69.3 [5.7] years; 3024 males [74.4%]) were included in the analysis. The median (IQR) follow-up was 11.8 (11.5-12.1) years. In models containing mortality risk factors (sociodemographic, behavioral, and health-related factors), higher clinical walking speed (HR, 0.77 [95% CI, 0.71-0.84]), median walking cadence (HR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.77-0.90]), and 95th percentile walking cadence (HR, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.75-0.89]) were associated with lower all-cause mortality risk (per 1 higher SD) and with a similar discriminative ability (clinical walking speed: C index, 0.747 [95% CI, 0.730-0.764]; median walking cadence: C index, 0.744 [95% CI, 0.726-0.761]; and 95th percentile walking cadence: C index, 0.745 [95% CI, 0.727-0.762]). Only clinical walking speed was associated with an improved discriminative ability of a model including mortality risk factors.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study, clinical walking speed and free-living walking cadence were both associated with all-cause mortality risk and had a similar discriminative ability for all-cause mortality. These results suggest that both measures can be used in population-based studies, and the choice between the 2 methods may depend on research objectives, implementation constraints, and the strengths of each method.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Longitudinal Change in Calf Circumference and Incident Falls in Older Adults
item.description:
Importance: Calf circumference (CC) is a simple, noninvasive proxy for lower-limb muscle mass. However, evidence on the longitudinal association between CC change and incident falls remains scarce.

Objective: To investigate whether progressive decline in CC is associated with higher odds of incident falls among community-dwelling older adults.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study used data from the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey, a nationally representative prospective cohort. Participants aged 60 years or older with complete CC measurements at baseline (2018) and follow-up (2021) were included. Data were analyzed from January to March 2026.

Exposures: Absolute CC change (in centimeters) and relative CC change (as a percentage) over 3 years, analyzed as continuous and categorical variables (absolute: no decrease, <3 cm, 3 to <5 cm, ≥5 cm; relative: no decrease, <10%, 10% to <20%, ≥20%). The no-decrease group, including individuals with no change and those with increased CC, served as the reference group.

Main outcomes and measures: The outcome of interest was incident falls, self-reported during the 2021 wave. Covariates included sociodemographic characteristics, falls history, health behaviors, functional status, and chronic diseases, all assessed via standardized questionnaires and evaluation. Odds of incident fall were assessed using inverse probability weighted logistic regression to address survival bias.

Results: Among 7068 participants (mean [SD] age, 79.66 [10.32] years; 3835 [54.26%] female), 1671 participants (23.64%) reported incident falls over a median (IQR) follow-up of 3.07 (2.91-3.17) years. In fully adjusted models, each 1-cm absolute decrease in CC was associated with 3.2% higher odds of fall (odds ratio [OR], 1.03; 95% CI, 1.02-1.05) and each 10% relative decrease with 10.3% higher odds (OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.15). Compared with no decrease, an absolute decrease in CC of 5 cm or more was associated with 32.5% higher odds of fall (OR, 1.33; 95% CI, 1.10-1.60) and a relative decrease of 20% or more with 48.1% higher odds (OR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.20-1.84).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of older adults, longitudinal decreases in CC, both absolute and relative, were associated with higher odds of incident falls. Monitoring CC change over time may serve as a practical, low-cost measure to support fall risk assessment.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Ultraprocessed Food Intake, Striatal Response to Food Cues, and Adiposity Gain in Children
item.description:
Importance: Preclinical studies suggest that ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) are associated with increased dopaminergic signaling in the striatum, reinforcing intake. Whether habitual UPF consumption is associated with striatal responses to food cues and subsequent adiposity gain in children is unknown.

Objective: To examine associations between habitual UPF intake, striatal responses to food cues, and 1-year adiposity changes in children.

Design, setting, and participants: This prospective cohort study included children of healthy weight who were participating in the longitudinal BrainChild study. Baseline assessments were completed between April 11, 2015, and June 28, 2024, and included brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), dietary recalls, and adiposity measurements. Additional follow-up assessments of adiposity were conducted 1 year later (April 18, 2016, to June 19, 2025).

Exposure: Habitual UPF intake, defined as the percentage of total energy intake from UPFs based on multiple 24-hour dietary recalls using the NOVA classification system.

Main outcomes and measures: Blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) responses to food cues in the dorsal and ventral striatum during functional MRI and 1-year changes in body mass index (BMI), body fat percentage, and waist circumference. Associations were examined using linear regression models and adjusted for age, sex, baseline BMI, and total caloric intake, with regression coefficient (β) reported as per SD change in outcome with per SD change in the exposure variable.

Results: In 46 children of healthy weight (mean [SD] age, 8.7 [1.1] years; 26 [57%] female; baseline BMI range, 13.8-19.9; body fat percentage range, 12.7%-32.2%), higher habitual UPF consumption was associated with greater BOLD responses to food cues in the dorsal striatum (β = 0.34; 95% CI, 0.07-0.61) but not the ventral striatum (β = 0.16; 95% CI, -0.14 to 0.46). Greater dorsal striatal food cue responsivity was associated with 1-year increases in BMI (β = 0.32; 95% CI, 0.02-0.62) and body fat percentage (β = 0.44; 95% CI, 0.15-0.72). Baseline UPF intake was associated with a 1-year increase in waist circumference (β = 0.38; 95% CI, 0.11-0.66). Point estimates for associations between UPF intake and increases in BMI (β = 0.28; 95% CI, 0.00-0.57) and body fat percentage (β = 0.29; 95% CI, 0.00-0.57) were positive. Inclusion of dorsal striatal responsivity attenuated the UPF associations with 1-year change in BMI by 31% and with body fat percentage by 44%.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of children of healthy weight, higher habitual UPF intake was associated with greater dorsal striatal responses to food cues and prospective increases in adiposity. These findings suggest that reward-related brain responses may be involved in associations between UPF consumption and adiposity gain during childhood.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Health Care Costs and Immigration Status Among US Adults
item.description:
Importance: The Affordable Care Act (ACA) expanded insurance coverage, while the 2018 Public Charge Rule Proposal (PCRP) raised concerns about immigration-related barriers to health care access.

Objective: To evaluate changes in insurance coverage, health care use, and medical expenditures among immigrant and US-born adults across ACA expansion and post-PCRP eras, stratified by poverty status.

Design, setting, and participants: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (2010-2023) data for US adults aged 19 to 64 years with available data on nativity, family income, insurance coverage, use, and expenditures. Income less than 138% of the federal poverty level was considered low income; 138% or higher was considered not low. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2026, to April 15, 2026.

Exposures: Policy era, categorized as pre-ACA expansion (2010-2013), post-ACA expansion (2014-2018), and post-PCRP (2019-2023), and nativity, categorized as immigrant or US-born.

Main outcomes and measures: Primary outcomes were person-year measures of insurance coverage, health care use, and annual medical expenditures adjusted to constant 2023 US dollars. Survey-weighted multivariable models estimated adjusted changes across eras and tested differences by nativity.

Results: Complete-case adjusted analyses included 237 175 person-year observations from 126 724 unique adults, including 67 076 female adults (50.8%) and 59 648 male adults (49.2%), with a survey-weighted mean (SD) age of 40.8 (13.2) years; the analytic sample included 56 561 low-income and 180 614 non-low-income person-year observations. Among adults with low income, post-PCRP insurance coverage was higher among US-born adults (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 2.84; 95% CI, 2.55-3.17) and immigrants (AOR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.98-2.65), with smaller relative gains for immigrants. Post-PCRP total expenditures increased among US-born adults with low income (β = $1684.60; 95% CI, $883.10-$2486.20) but not among immigrants with low income (β = $220.20; 95% CI, -$680.10-$1120.50). Among adults without low income, post-PCRP total expenditures increased among US-born adults (β = $1788.60; 95% CI, $1487.70-$2089.50) and immigrants (β = $974.10; 95% CI, $517.50-$1430.70).

Conclusions and relevance: In this serial cross-sectional study of US adults aged 19 to 64 years, immigrants had lower insurance coverage, health care use, and medical expenditures than US-born adults. Coverage was higher in later eras, but coverage gains and expenditure growth were smaller among immigrants with low income, suggesting that insurance expansion alone may be insufficient to address nativity-related differences in health care access and spending.

Alizai Q, Arena L, Mevawalla A, Ejaz R, Zih-Shou JW, Angez M

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Race- and Neighborhood-Level Social Determinants of Health in Diagnosis and Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation
item.description:
Importance: Early diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF) is critical for preventing stroke, heart failure, and mortality. Understanding patterns in diagnosis and treatment of AF may improve detection and reduce disparities.

Objective: To evaluate the interactions between race and ethnicity and neighborhood social determinants of health on AF diagnosis and treatment.

Design, setting, and participants: Retrospective cohort study using administrative claims for greater Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, area residents aged 18 years or older from Independence Blue Cross from 2017 to 2021. Baseline characteristics were assessed in 2017, and participants were followed up from 2018 through 2021. Data were analyzed from October 2023 to July 2026.

Exposures: Exposures included Non-Hispanic Black race and ethnicity, neighborhood-level social determinants of health as measured by the social barrier index (SBI), and the interaction between the two.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was AF diagnosis ascertained from International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision diagnosis codes. The secondary outcome was anticoagulant prescription among individuals with AF diagnoses as ascertained from pharmacy claims.

Results: Of the 504 876 patients included, the mean (SD) age was 48 (18) years; 267 596 (53.0%) were female; 67 362 (13.3%) non-Hispanic Black, and 437 514 (86.7%) were non-Hispanic White. A total of 27 249 patients (5.1%) were diagnosed with AF during the study period. Non-Hispanic Black patients were less likely to be diagnosed with AF compared with non-Hispanic White patients (odds ratio [OR], 0.91; 95% CI, 0.82-1.00). The relative difference increased with increased SBI (which denotes more vulnerable neighborhoods) as shown by a significant interaction between race and ethnicity and SBI (OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.86-0.95). Among those diagnosed with AF, 15 722 (58%) had an anticoagulant prescription. There was a significant interaction between race and ethnicity and SBI (OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.00-1.20), suggesting that filled prescription patterns differed by race and ethnicity with SBI. For Black individuals one unit increase in SBI was associated with decreased odds of AF diagnosis (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.90-0.99). For White individuals one unit increase in SBI was associated with increased odds of AF diagnosis (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.03-1.07).

Conclusions and relevance: This cohort study of Medicare Advantage and commercially insured individuals found that AF diagnosis rates declined with worsening neighborhood-level disadvantage among non-Hispanic Black individuals but increased among non-Hispanic White individuals. Conditional on diagnoses, rates of prescription of anticoagulants were similar across race and ethnicity groups. Targeted interventions, especially in more marginalized neighborhoods, are needed to increase detection of AF.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Trends in Direct Oral Anticoagulant Use for Cancer-Associated Venous Thromboembolism
item.description:
Importance: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) are recommended for selected patients with cancer-associated venous thromboembolism, but their implementation remains heterogeneous.

Objective: To describe temporal trends in DOAC initiation for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism in France and to identify factors associated with their use.

Design, setting, and participants: This nationwide population-based cohort study included adults without recorded contraindications to DOACs and a first treated venous thromboembolism episode between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2022. Data were collected from the French National Health Data System, a nationwide claims database covering approximately 99% of the population. Analysis was performed from January to August 2025.

Exposures: Patients were classified into active cancer and no active cancer groups. Covariates included calendar period, patient characteristics, cancer type and treatment, venous thromboembolism characteristics, and initial prescriber setting.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was DOAC initiation within 30 days after the index venous thromboembolism event. Bayesian structural time series models assessed temporal changes across 2016 to 2018, 2019 to 2020, and 2021 to 2022. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with DOAC initiation among patients with active cancer.

Results: Among 683 184 patients with incident treated venous thromboembolism (median [IQR] age, 67 [53-77] years; 347 421 female [51.0%]), 91 954 patients (13.5%) had active cancer while 591 230 (86.5%) had VTE not associated with active cancer. DOAC use increased from 15.3% (95% CI, 15.0%-15.7%) in 2016 to 2018 to 32.6% (95% CI, 32.1%-33.2%) in 2021 to 2022 among patients with active cancer, and from 63.5% (95% CI, 63.3%-63.7%) to 81.1% (95% CI, 80.9%-81.2%) among patients without active cancer. DOAC initiation increased beyond expected secular trends in patients with active cancer, with relative increases of 20.5% (95% credible interval, 13.0%-27.8%) in 2019 to 2020 and 41.3% (95% credible interval, 32.9%-50.2%) in 2021 to 2022. DOAC initiation was less frequent among patients with comorbidities, history of bleeding, gastrointestinal or gynecologic cancer, active brain metastases, or systemic treatment, and when the initial prescriber was a hospital-based physician rather than a general practitioner.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of patients with incident venous thromboembolism, DOAC use increased substantially in patients with active cancer but remained lower than in patients without active cancer and varied across clinical and care-setting characteristics. This lower uptake may reflect both delayed implementation of recent evidence and the need to individualize anticoagulant selection in complex situations.

Varnier R, Bettega F, Moskal A, Mainbourg S, Wespiser M, Rousseau A

item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: Community Paramedics Addressing the Evolving Opioid Crisis: A Case Series Addressing the Kratom Derivatives 7-Hydroxymitragynine and MGM-15
item.description:
Concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and dihydro-7-hydroxymitragynine (MGM-15) are derived from the primary psychoactive alkaloid in kratom, and until recently were sold over the counter with kratom products. These highly potent kratom derivatives can produce opioid-like dependence, but evidence around prehospital treatment of 7-OH and MGM-15 withdrawal symptoms remains limited. This case series assesses two cases of community paramedics (CPs) providing treatment and linkage to care for individuals in acute opioid withdrawal from 7-OH and MGM-15. In our first case a 74-year-old individual called 9-1-1 experiencing acute opioid-like withdrawal symptoms after abruptly discontinuing over the counter 7-OH following six months of progressively escalating use. Connection was made with a prehospital buprenorphine program (PBAP) and the CP administered 24mg of buprenorphine and expedited connection to outpatient treatment with medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD). Our second case involved a 38-year-old individual who called a CP requesting expedited linkage to MOUD following a period of escalating use of 7-OH and MGM-15. This patient was linked to MOUD treatment within 48 hours of contacting the CP and required 32mg/8mg of buprenorphine/naloxone to treat severe opioid withdrawal symptoms after discontinued use of MGM-15 tablets. Both patients were retained in MOUD treatment at 30 days. These cases describe use of CP-based PBAPs addressing severe 7-OH withdrawal and expediting treatment to outpatient MOUD, highlighting that concentrated over the counter 7-OH products can produce physical opioid dependence leading to opioid use disorder, and requiring full-dose buprenorphine induction which may be considered within existing prehospital opioid withdrawal treatment protocols. Additional research is necessary to characterize withdrawal from concentrated 7-OH products and to determine implications for PBAP protocols and 7-OH dosing in the United States.

item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: Rapid Transport to Extracorporeal CPR: Urging Caution Prior to Implementation
item.description:
Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has survival that remains near 10% despite years of research and advancements in care. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has been explored as an option for patients who suffer OHCA and are refractory to traditional therapies. In nearly every system that implements ECPR for OHCA, there is a requirement to incorporate intra-arrest transport (IAT). There are three major randomized controlled trials which have evaluated the role of ECPR in OHCA. These include ARREST, INCEPTION, and Prague OHCA. While ARREST has the strongest data to support ECPR, it includes only 30 patients. The larger trials such as INCEPTION and Prague OHCA did not show statistically significant results in favor of ECPR. Each trial has a unique study design and statistical analysis.The current evidence is not strong enough to support widespread adoption of ECPR into the prehospital systems of care. Examining the statistical pitfalls, potential biases, and methodological confounders of the existing ECPR literature against the background of previously reported data surrounding IAT─the full impact of effect of ECPR cannot exclude consideration of the impact of the effect of IAT. As more data is needed to better understand the full impact of implementing ECPR into a system of care, we encourage caution and thoughtful analysis to leaders who may be considering the addition of ECPR into an existing system of care. ECPR shows early promise for select patients. The development of an ECPR system is complex and has numerous facets, typically including the incorporation of early IAT for OHCA. At this time, more studies are needed on the full impacts of implementing ECPR into a system of care for OHCA.

Kimbrell JM, Kreinbrook JA, Robinson AE, Bunting AJ, Ambur S, Prekker ME

item.title: JAMA Intern Med: Video Decision Support and Advance Care Planning in Older Adults With Advanced Kidney Disease: The VIDEO-KD Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Older adults with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) face consequential decisions about whether to initiate dialysis, yet advance care planning (ACP), the communication that prepares patients for such decisions, is documented infrequently in ambulatory settings.

Objective: To determine whether a video decision aid about treatment options for advanced CKD, combined with patient-created video declarations, increases ACP documentation among older adults with advanced CKD.

Design, setting, and participants: This multicenter, parallel-group randomized clinical trial was conducted at 12 ambulatory clinics from June 2021 to March 2025, with 12-month follow-up. Participants were adults 65 years or older with advanced CKD. Outcome assessors were masked to group assignment. Data were analyzed in April 2026.

Interventions: Intervention participants viewed a certified video decision aid depicting 3 treatment options for advanced CKD (hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and conservative kidney management) and then created a video declaration, a recorded statement of goals, values, and treatment preferences in video, audio, or written format, that was sent to their treating clinician. Control participants received usual medical care.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was ACP documentation in the electronic health record within 12 months of enrollment or death, whichever came sooner. Documentation was ascertained by validated natural language processing-assisted human adjudication. Prespecified secondary outcomes included documented discussion of kidney failure treatment options and stated treatment preferences.

Results: A total of 453 patients were included (228 intervention [50.3%] and 225 control [49.7%]; mean [SD] age, 78.8 [6.4] years; 190 women [41.9%]; 4 American Indian or Alaska Native [1.1%], 8 Asian [1.8%], 38 Black [8.4%], 35 Hispanic or Latino [7.7%], 3 Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander [0.7%], and 375 White [82.8%] individuals). At 12 months, ACP documentation was higher in the intervention group than the control group (56.6% vs 40.0%; rate difference, 16.6%; 95% CI, 7.5%-25.7%; P < .001), as was documented discussion of kidney failure treatment options (46.1% vs 31.6%; rate difference, 14.5%; 95% CI, 5.6%-23.4%; P = .001). After viewing the video, fewer intervention participants than controls at enrollment were undecided about treatment (30 of 227 [13.2%] vs 92 of 223 [41.3%]), and more preferred conservative kidney management (115 of 227 [50.7%] vs 71 of 223 [31.8%]; P < .001 for the overall distribution).

Conclusions and relevance: This randomized clinical trial found that, among older adults with advanced CKD, a video decision aid increased ACP documentation and reduced the proportion of patients who were undecided about treatment.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04347629.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Low Daily Protein Intake and Risk of Kidney Failure and Mortality in Chronic Kidney Disease
item.description:
Importance: While protein restriction is a cornerstone of chronic kidney disease (CKD) management, its long-term benefits on clinical outcomes in Asian populations, who often have lower body mass and muscle reserves, remain unclear.

Objective: To investigate the association between daily protein intake (DPI) and the risk of kidney failure requiring replacement therapy (KFRT) and all-cause mortality in patients with non-dialysis-dependent CKD.

Design, setting, and participants: This prospective cohort study used data from the Korean Cohort Study for Outcomes in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease (KNOW-CKD). Participants with CKD at stages ranging from 1 to predialysis 5 were enrolled between 2011 and 2016 from 9 tertiary hospitals in South Korea. The study observation period ended on January 31, 2024. Data analysis was performed from February 2024 to May 2026.

Exposures: DPI was objectively estimated using 24-hour urinary nitrogen excretion at baseline. The participants were categorized by DPI: less than 0.6, 0.6 to less than 0.8, 0.8 to less than 1.0, 1.0 to less than 1.2, and 1.2 or greater.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was the onset of KFRT. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were used to account for the competing risk of death.

Results: A total of 1861 participants (mean [SD] age, 53.7 [12.0] years; 1304 [61.1%] male) were analyzed, with a median (range) follow-up of 9.3 (0.01-12.37) years. The lowest DPI group (<0.6 g/kg/d) was associated with increased risk of KFRT (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.42; 95% CI, 1.09-1.85) as well as all-cause mortality (sHR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.17-4.03), but not MACEs, compared with the highest DPI group (>1.2 g/kg/d). Furthermore, a nonlinear association was observed, where excessively low protein intake was associated with an increased risk of KFRT.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of 1861 patients with nondialysis CKD, low protein intake was not associated with significant nephroprotection and was associated with a higher risk of KFRT and all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that rigid protein restriction should be balanced with nutritional monitoring to prevent protein-energy wasting, particularly in populations with lower muscle mass, and a more individualized approach to dietary protein management in CKD may be warranted.

Suh SH, Choi HS, Kim CS, Bae EH, Kim J, Jung JY
Journal Article
